verses.zh: 你们的　神说：你们要安慰，安慰我的百姓。
verses.en: “Comfort, comfort my people,” says your[NOTE:1] God.
notes: The pronominal suffix is second masculine plural. The identity of the addressee is uncertain: (1) God’s people may be addressed, or (2) the unidentified heralds commanded to comfort Jerusalem.

verses.zh: 要对耶路撒冷说安慰的话，又向她宣告说，她争战的日子已满了；她的罪孽赦免了；她为自己的一切罪，从耶和华手中加倍受罚。
verses.en: “Speak kindly to[NOTE:1] Jerusalem[NOTE:2] and tell herthat her time of warfare is over,[NOTE:3] that her punishment is completed.[NOTE:4] For the Lord has made her pay double[NOTE:5] for all her sins.”
notes: Heb “speak to the heart of Jerusalem.” Jerusalem is personified as a woman.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “that she is filled [with] her warfare.” Some understand צָבָא (tsavah, “warfare”) as meaning “hard service” or “compulsory labor” in this context.
Heb “that her punishment is accepted [as satisfactory].”

Heb “for she has received from the hand of the Lord double.” The principle of the double portion in punishment is also seen in Jer 16:18; 17:18 and Rev 18:6. For examples of the double portion in Israelite law, see Exod 22:4, 7, 9 (double restitution by a thief) and Deut 21:17 (double inheritance portion for the firstborn).

verses.zh: 有人声喊着说：在旷野预备耶和华的路（或译：在旷野，有人声喊着说：当预备耶和华的路），在沙漠地修平我们　神的道。
verses.en: A voice cries out,“In the wilderness clear a way for the Lord;build a level road[NOTE:1] through the rift valley[NOTE:2] for our God.
notes: Heb “make level a built road.” The verb יָשַׁר (yashar) in the Piel means “to make smooth, or straight.” The noun מְסִלָּה (mesillah) typically refers to a main road, possibly paved with stones or made level with fill (see HALOT 606 s.v. and The Concise DCH 230 s.v.).

Most translations render this as “desert” (KJV, NASB, ESV, NRSV, NIV11, HCSB), “wilderness” (NIV84), or “wasteland” (NLV). The rift valley (עֲרָבָה, ʿaravah), which extends from Galilee to the Gulf of Aqaba, is quite arid and desert-like in the areas near the Dead Sea and southward (see the note at Num 22:1). But the point here has more to do with preparation for a royal visit. To come to Jerusalem from the east requires coming through the rift valley (or Jordan Valley). Thematically, God is typically portrayed as coming to Israel from the east. Similarly in the Gospel accounts Jesus approaches Jerusalem from the east.

verses.zh: 一切山洼都要填满，大小山冈都要削平；高高低低的要改为平坦，崎崎岖岖的必成为平原。
verses.en: Every valley must be elevatedand every mountain and hill leveled.The rough terrain will become a level plain,the rugged landscape a wide valley.

verses.zh: 耶和华的荣耀必然显现；凡有血气的必一同看见；因为这是耶和华亲口说的。
verses.en: The splendor[NOTE:1] of the Lord will be revealed,and all people[NOTE:2] will see it at the same time.For[NOTE:3] the Lord has decreed it.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “glory.” The Lord’s “glory” is his theophanic radiance and royal splendor (see Isa 6:3; 24:23; 35:2; 60:1; 66:18-19).
Heb “flesh” (so KJV, ASV, NASB); NAB, NIV84 “mankind”; NIV11 “people”; TEV “the whole human race.”
Or “indeed.”
Heb “the mouth of the Lord has spoken” (so NASB, NIV, NRSV).

verses.zh: 有人声说：你喊叫吧！有一个说：我喊叫甚么呢？说：凡有血气的尽都如草；他的美容都像野地的花。
verses.en: A voice says, “Cry out!”Another asks,[NOTE:1] “What should I cry out?”The first voice responds:[NOTE:2] “All people are like grass,[NOTE:3] and all their promises[NOTE:4] are like the flowers in the field.
notes: Heb “and he says.” Apparently a second “voice” responds to the command of the first “voice.”
The words “the first voice responds” are supplied in the translation for clarification. The first voice tells the second one what to declare.
Heb “all flesh is grass.” The point of the metaphor is explained in v. 7.

Heb “and all his loyalty.” The antecedent of the third masculine suffix is בָּשָׂר (basar, “flesh”), which refers collectively to mankind. The LXX, apparently understanding the antecedent as “grass,” reads “glory,” but חֶסֶד (khesed) rarely, if ever, has this nuance. The normal meaning of חֶסֶד (“faithfulness, loyalty, devotion”) fits very well in the argument. Human beings and their faithfulness (verbal expressions of faithfulness are specifically in view; cf. NRSV “constancy”) are short-lived and unreliable, in stark contrast to the decrees and promises of the eternal God.

verses.zh: 草必枯干，花必凋残，因为耶和华的气吹在其上；百姓诚然是草。
verses.en: The grass dries up,the flowers wither,when the wind sent by the Lord[NOTE:1] blows on them.Surely humanity[NOTE:2] is like grass.
notes: The Hebrew text has רוּחַ יְהוָה (ruakh yehvah), which in this context probably does not refer to the Lord’s personal Spirit. The phrase is better translated “the breath of the Lord,” or “the wind of [i.e., sent by] the Lord.” The Lord’s sovereign control over nature, including the hot desert winds that dry up vegetation, is in view here (cf. Ps 147:18; Isa 59:19).
Heb “the people” (so KJV, ASV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV).

verses.zh: 草必枯干，花必凋残，惟有我们　神的话必永远立定。
verses.en: The grass dries up,the flowers wither,but the decree of our God is forever reliable.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “but the word of our God stands forever.” In this context the divine “word” specifically refers to his decreed promise assuring Jerusalem that her suffering is over and his glorious return imminent (vv. 1-5).

verses.zh: 报好信息给锡安的啊，你要登高山；报好信息给耶路撒冷的啊，你要极力扬声。扬声不要惧怕，对犹大的城邑说：看哪，你们的　神！
verses.en: Go up on a high mountain, O herald Zion.Shout out loudly, O herald Jerusalem![NOTE:1] Shout, don’t be afraid!Say to the towns of Judah,“Here is your God!”
notes: The second feminine singular imperatives are addressed to personified Zion/Jerusalem, who is here told to ascend a high hill and proclaim the good news of the Lord’s return to the other towns of Judah. Isa 41:27 and 52:7 speak of a herald sent to Zion, but the masculine singular form מְבַשֵּׂר (mevasser) is used in these verses, in contrast to the feminine singular form מְבַשֶּׂרֶת (mevasseret) employed in 40:9, where Zion is addressed as a herald.

verses.zh: 主耶和华必像大能者临到；他的膀臂必为他掌权。他的赏赐在他那里；他的报应在他面前。
verses.en: Look, the Sovereign Lord comes as a victorious warrior;[NOTE:1] his military power establishes his rule.[NOTE:2] Look, his reward is with him;his prize goes before him.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “comes as a strong one”; ASV “will come as a mighty one.” The preposition בְּ (bet) here carries the nuance “in the capacity of.” It indicates that the Lord possesses the quality expressed by the noun. See GKC 379 §119.i and HALOT 104 s.v. בְּ.
Heb “his arm rules for him” (so NIV84, NRSV); NIV11 “he rules with a mighty arm.” The Lord’s “arm” symbolizes his military power (see Isa 51:9-10; 63:5).

As the Lord returns to Jerusalem as a victorious warrior, he brings with him the spoils of victory, called here his “reward” and “prize.” These terms might also be translated “wages” and “recompense.” Verse 11 indicates that his rescued people, likened to a flock of sheep, are his reward.

verses.zh: 他必像牧人牧养自己的羊群，用膀臂聚集羊羔抱在怀中，慢慢引导那乳养小羊的。
verses.en: Like a shepherd he tends his flock;he gathers up the lambs with his arm;he carries them close to his heart;[NOTE:1] he leads the ewes along.
notes: Heb “in his bosom” (so KJV, NAB, NASB, NRSV), an expression which reflects closeness and protective care.

verses.zh: 谁曾用手心量诸水，用手虎口量苍天，用升斗盛大地的尘土，用秤称山岭，用天平平冈陵呢？
verses.en: Who has measured out the waters[NOTE:1] in the hollow of his hand,or carefully[NOTE:2] measured the sky,[NOTE:3] or carefully weighed[NOTE:4] the soil of the earth,or weighed the mountains in a balance,or the hills on scales?[NOTE:5]
notes: The Qumran scroll 1QIsaa has מי ים (“waters of the sea”), a reading followed by NAB.
Heb “with a span.” A “span” was the distance between the ends of the thumb and the little finger of the spread hand” (BDB 285 s.v. זֶרֶת).
Or “the heavens.” The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heavens” or “sky” depending on the context.
Heb “or weighed by a third part [of a measure].”

The implied answer to the rhetorical questions of v. 12 is, “No one but the Lord.” The Lord, and no other, created the world. Like a merchant weighing out silver or commodities on a scale, the Lord established the various components of the physical universe in precise proportions.

verses.zh: 谁曾测度耶和华的心（或译：谁曾指示耶和华的灵），或作他的谋士指教他呢？
verses.en: Who comprehends[NOTE:1] the mind[NOTE:2] of the Lord,or gives him instruction as his counselor?[NOTE:3]
notes: Perhaps the verb is used metonymically here in the sense of “advises” (note the following line).
In this context רוּחַ (ruakh) likely refers to the Lord’s “mind,” or mental faculties, rather than his personal Spirit (see BDB 925 s.v. 6).
Heb “or [as] the man of his counsel causes him to know?”

verses.zh: 他与谁商议，谁教导他，谁将公平的路指示他，又将知识教训他，将通达的道指教他呢？
verses.en: From whom does he receive directions?[NOTE:1] Who[NOTE:2] teaches him the correct way to do things,[NOTE:3] or imparts knowledge to him,or instructs him in skillful design?[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “With whom did he consult, so that he gave discernment to him?”
Heb “and taught him.” The vav (ו) consecutive with prefixed verbal form continues the previous line. The translation employs an interrogative pronoun for stylistic reasons.

The phrase אֹרַח מִשְׁפָּט (ʾorakh mishpat) could be translated “path of justice” (so NASB, NRSV), but in this context, where creative ability and skill is in view, the phrase is better understood in the sense of “the way that is proper or fitting” (see BDB 1049 s.v. מִשְׁפָּט 6); cf. NIV, NCV “the right way.”

Heb “or the way of understanding causes him to know?”sn The implied answer to the rhetorical questions in vv. 13-14 is, “No one.” In contrast to Marduk, the creator-god of Mesopotamian myths who receives help from the god of wisdom, the Lord neither needs nor receives any such advice or help. See R. Whybray, Heavenly Counsellor (SOTSMS), 64-77.

verses.zh: 看哪，万民都像水桶的一滴，又算如天平上的微尘；他举起众海岛，好像极微之物。
verses.en: Look, the nations are like a drop in a bucket;they are regarded as dust on the scales.He lifts[NOTE:1] the coastlands[NOTE:2] as if they were dust.
notes: Or “weighs” (NIV); NLT “picks up.”
Or “islands” (NASB, NIV, NLT).

verses.zh: 黎巴嫩的树林不够当柴烧；其中的走兽也不够作燔祭。
verses.en: Not even Lebanon could supply enough firewood for a sacrifice;[NOTE:1] its wild animals would not provide enough burnt offerings.[NOTE:2]
notes: The words “for a sacrifice” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
The point is that not even the Lebanon forest could supply enough wood and animals for an adequate sacrifice to the Lord.

verses.zh: 万民在他面前好像虚无，被他看为不及虚无，乃为虚空。
verses.en: All the nations are insignificant before him;they are regarded as absolutely nothing.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “[as derived] from nothing and unformed.”

verses.zh: 你们究竟将谁比　神，用甚么形像与　神比较呢？
verses.en: To whom can you compare God?To what image can you liken him?

verses.zh: 偶像是匠人铸造，银匠用金包裹，为它铸造银链。
verses.en: A craftsman casts[NOTE:1] an idol;a metalsmith overlays it with goldand forges silver chains for it.
notes: Heb “pours out”; KJV “melteth.”

verses.zh: 穷乏献不起这样供物的，就拣选不能朽坏的树木，为自己寻找巧匠，立起不能摇动的偶像。
verses.en: To make a contribution one selects wood that will not rot;[NOTE:1] he then seeks a skilled craftsmanto make[NOTE:2] an idol that will not fall over.
notes: The first two words of the verse (הַמְסֻכָּן תְּרוּמָה, hamesukkan terumah) are problematic. Some take מְסֻכָּן as an otherwise unattested Pual participle from סָכַן (sakhan, “be poor”) and translate “the one who is impoverished.” תְּרוּמָה (terumah, “contribution”) can then be taken as an adverbial accusative, “with respect to a contribution,” and the entire line translated, “the one who is too impoverished for such a contribution [i.e., the metal idol of v. 19?] selects wood that will not rot.” However, מְסֻכָּן is probably the name of a tree used in idol manufacturing (cognate with Akkadian musukkanu, cf. H. R. Cohen, Biblical Hapax Legomena [SBLDS], 133). מְסֻכָּן may be a scribal interpretive addition attempting to specify עֵץ (ʿets) or עֵץ may be a scribal attempt to categorize מְסֻכָּן. How an idol constitutes a תְּרוּמָה (“contribution”) is not entirely clear.
Or “set up” (ASV, NAB, NIV, NRSV); KJV, NASB “to prepare.”

verses.zh: 你们岂不曾知道吗？你们岂不曾听见吗？从起初岂没有人告诉你们吗？自从立地的根基，你们岂没有明白吗？
verses.en: Do you not know?Do you not hear?Has it not been told to you since the very beginning?Have you not understood from the time the earth’s foundations were made?

verses.zh: 神坐在地球大圈之上；地上的居民好像蝗虫。他铺张穹苍如幔子，展开诸天如可住的帐棚。
verses.en: He is the one who sits on the earth’s horizon;[NOTE:1] its inhabitants are like grasshoppers before him.[NOTE:2] He is the one who stretches out the sky like a thin curtain,[NOTE:3] and spreads it out[NOTE:4] like a pitched tent.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “the circle of the earth” (so KJV, NIV, NRSV, NLT).
The words “before him” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

The otherwise unattested noun דֹּק (doq), translated here “thin curtain,” is apparently derived from the verbal root דקק (“crush”) from which is derived the adjective דַּק (daq, “thin”; see HALOT 229 s.v. דקק). The nuance “curtain” is implied from the parallelism (see “tent” in the next line).

The meaning of the otherwise unattested verb מָתַח (matakh, “spread out”) is determined from the parallelism (note the corresponding verb “stretch out” in the previous line) and supported by later Hebrew and Aramaic cognates. See HALOT 654 s.v. *מתה.
Heb “like a tent [in which] to live”; NAB, NASB “like a tent to dwell (live NIV, NRSV) in.”

verses.zh: 他使君王归于虚无，使地上的审判官成为虚空。
verses.en: He is the one who reduces rulers to nothing;he makes the earth’s leaders insignificant.

verses.zh: 他们是刚才（或译：不曾；下同）栽上，刚才种上，根也刚才扎在地里，他一吹在其上，便都枯干；旋风将他们吹去，像碎秸一样。
verses.en: Indeed, they are barely planted;yes, they are barely sown;yes, they barely take root in the earth,and then he blows on them, causing them to dry up,and the wind carries them away like straw.

verses.zh: 那圣者说：你们将谁比我，叫他与我相等呢？
verses.en: “To whom can you compare me? Whom do I resemble?”says the Holy One.[NOTE:1]
notes: See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.

verses.zh: 你们向上举目，看谁创造这万象，按数目领出，他一一称其名；因他的权能，又因他的大能大力，连一个都不缺。
verses.en: Look up at the sky![NOTE:1] Who created all these heavenly lights?[NOTE:2] He is the one who leads out their ranks;[NOTE:3] he calls them all by name.Because of his absolute power and awesome strength,not one of them is missing.
notes: Heb “Lift on high your eyes and see.”
The words “heavenly lights” are supplied in the translation for clarification. See the following lines.

Heb “the one who brings out by number their host.” The stars are here likened to a huge army that the Lord leads out. Perhaps the next line pictures God calling roll. If so, the final line may be indicating that none of them dares “go AWOL.” (“AWOL” is a military acronym for “absent without leave.”)

verses.zh: 雅各啊，你为何说，我的道路向耶和华隐藏？以色列啊，你为何言，我的冤屈　神并不查问？
verses.en: Why do you say, Jacob,Why do you say, Israel,“The Lord is not aware of what is happening to me;[NOTE:1] my God is not concerned with my vindication”?[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “my way is hidden from the Lord” (so NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV).
Heb “and from my God my justice passes away”; NRSV “my right is disregarded by my God.”

verses.zh: 你岂不曾知道吗？你岂不曾听见吗？永在的　神耶和华，创造地极的主，并不疲乏，也不困倦；他的智慧无法测度。
verses.en: Do you not know?Have you not heard?The Lord is an eternal God,the Creator of the whole earth.[NOTE:1] He does not get tired or weary;there is no limit to his wisdom.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the ends of the earth,” but this is a merism, where the earth’s extremities stand for its entirety, i.e., the extremities and everything in between them.

Exiled Israel’s complaint (v. 27) implies that God might be limited in some way. Perhaps he, like so many of the pagan gods, has died. Or perhaps his jurisdiction is limited to Judah and does not include Babylon. Maybe he is unable to devise an adequate plan to rescue his people, or is unable to execute it. But v. 28 affirms that he is not limited temporally or spatially nor are his power and wisdom restricted in any way. He can and will deliver his people, if they respond in hopeful faith (v. 31a).

verses.zh: 疲乏的，他赐能力；软弱的，他加力量。
verses.en: He gives strength to those who are tired;to the ones who lack power, he gives renewed energy.

verses.zh: 就是少年人也要疲乏困倦；强壮的也必全然跌倒。
verses.en: Even youths get tired and weary;even strong young men clumsily stumble.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “stumbling they stumble.” The verbal idea is emphasized by the infinitive absolute.

verses.zh: 但那等候耶和华的必重新得力。他们必如鹰展翅上腾；他们奔跑却不困倦，行走却不疲乏。
verses.en: But those who wait for the Lord’s help[NOTE:1] find renewed strength;they rise up as if they had eagles’ wings,[NOTE:2] they run without growing weary,they walk without getting tired.
notes: The word “help” in the phrase “for the Lord’s help” is supplied in the translation for clarification, as is the possessive on “Lord.”
Heb “they rise up [on] wings like eagles” (TEV similar).
